design.execution_model: 20 pairs (10 tasks x 2 families), 2 arms each = 40 executions, interleaved (two family streams in parallel, frozen per-family order, frozen per-pair arm order)
design.harder_bar: each task requires reading EXISTING code across >=2 files in the target repo before any correct change (multi-file composition/parity work, not single-function specs); frozen objective acceptance authored BEFORE any run; no human judgment
design.verification: masked verify_arm (task + worktree only): claim file + grounding-unchanged-vs-pin + frozen acceptance + participant validation; arm-attributable no-output is Y=0

diagnostic_label: G3 rev2 feasibility pilot (harder tasks) - DIAGNOSTIC SCREEN ONLY. NOT Gate G3, NOT protocol evidence, NO gate claims, NO promotion authority. A yes/no screen for whether a proper G3 rev2 is worth authoring.

discrimination_readout.detail: Zero discrimination. All 40 arms passed (Y=1): fam-gpt static 10/10 vs evidence 10/10; fam-glm static 10/10 vs evidence 10/10. No pair split; no task showed any static-vs-evidence difference; mean arm durations are also indistinguishable (fam-gpt 292s vs 274s, fam-glm 269s vs 272s). The closed campaign's ceiling effect (easy tasks, arms identical at 91.7%/91.7% gpt and 100%/100% grok) REPRODUCES at a substantially harder bar: exact reproduction of a seeded k-means (RNG call sequence, tie-breaking, centroid re-normalization), byte-identical packet rendering across 4 files, multi-module parity compositions. Both executors solved every task with or without the engineering-core advice payload.
discrimination_readout.question: on HARDER tasks grounded in real softwareco/owned repos, do the static and evidence arms separate AT ALL?
discrimination_readout.rev2_implication: A proper G3 rev2 at this difficulty band is NOT worth authoring: tasks requiring multi-file reading and faithful re-implementation still saturate both arms. Any rev2 that wants discrimination must change the task class (e.g., tasks the advice surface is specifically built to inform, longer-horizon or repository-wide work, or failure-prone integration work), not merely raise per-task reading difficulty. This is a pilot readout, not a gate decision.
discrimination_readout.secondary_observation: fam-glm (zai/glm-5.3:high) matched fam-gpt (openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol:high) exactly on this corpus (both 20/20 arms); the corpus was also at ceiling for BOTH families.
